title: Wrinkly fingers aren't soggy skin
topic: Why do fingers wrinkle in water?

lines: Wrinkly bath fingers aren't soggy skin. They're your nervous system at work.
When your hands soak, nerves tell the blood vessels in your fingertips to narrow.
The padding underneath shrinks, and the skin folds into ridges.
Patients with nerve damage soaked their hands, and their fingers stayed perfectly smooth.

beats.label: faster moving wet marbles
lines: So why bother? A Newcastle study found people moved wet marbles twelve percent faster with wrinkly fingers.
But a year later, a Berlin team tested forty people and found no grip advantage at all.
So the wrinkles are real, and your nerves make them.
Why they exist? Scientists are still arguing.

sources.claim: Wrinkling is caused by the sympathetic nervous system narrowing blood vessels; 1936 patients with nerve damage stayed smooth
2013 Newcastle study: 12% faster with wet marbles when wrinkled
2014 Berlin MDC study of 40 volunteers found no grip advantage
